fix(doctor): a failed run notes its reason, every turn's record reaches the CLI's wait, and the doctor's fields are pairs the record's writer quotes (9a7)

From the step-10 review:
- A run whose reading failed notes `failed` with its reason on its turn's
  record, so `cc-candybar doctor` says why at once instead of timing out.
- The doctor's field groups are key/value pairs written by the one logfmt
  writer, so a terminal release with a space in it no longer fails the run.
- A link click judged on a run asked another way proves the URL handler.
- rendererHost hands every turn's record to a `recorded` sink, so a note on a
  turn the host took itself (a due, a config turn, a start) reaches a wait.
- The faults note is made as its record is kept, so a draw that throws notes
  nothing a later `kept` is read against, and each frame spells it once.
- The doctor CLI's bar closes as the first teardown step, and a step that
  fails to close is the command's failure on stderr.
- postMortemsOf has its doc comment back; the zones test's root fixtures
  name a file still a root.

docs(memory): check and the doctor command draw through answer, and the doctor CLI never asks a daemon (9a7)

The memory lines that said check composes its own payload, that the CLI
reads the doctor's stores through the daemon, and how the deleted URL probe
chose its socket now say what holds: both commands are hosts of their own
over the daemon's collector and host, the doctor CLI reads the profile's
stores itself and names the facts only a running daemon holds as not judged
here, and each check pass is a session of its own so its first record
carries every fault.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(doctor): the doctor command is a host of its own bar and asks no daemon (9a7)

`cc-candybar doctor` stands up a local bar of the daemon's parts over the
session's own discovery, stored state and payload owners, draws its bar,
then sends the renderer a `doctor-run` click that arrives by command. The
renderer judges the run through the daemon's DoctorSource and notes every
check's verdict on that turn's record; the command prints the note. A run
whose note never comes is a loud exit 2.

DoctorSource takes what its host saw of a session as a provider: the daemon
hands it its render sightings and itself, the command its one drawn bar,
its own width, and not-held for what only a running daemon knows. A check
over a fact not held is ok with a note naming the bar's doctor as its judge;
the daemon check still judges the process table and unread post-mortems, and
the URL handler check reads the scheme's registration from Launch Services.

The daemon-stats doctor answer, the handler probe and its click verb, the
doctor's stats fields and the `doctor:` log line go. The doctor's record
fields are each one logfmt value, so a font or terminal name is read whole.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(check): check draws every preset's bar through the daemon's own host and renderer (9a7)

`check` stands up a local bar of the daemon's parts: a collector over the
fixture session's owners, the main renderer in process, the renderer host
and the statusline answer. Each preset is one stored session whose pick is
that preset, drawn by one render request through the request checkpoint, and
the verdict reads the request turn's record: its faults, the preset it drew
and the sources still unread when its wait ended. A turn that threw, or an
answer with no frame, is a `render:` failure.

The faked session owns where its directory sits, so the host's location read
is a port: the daemon's is the disk, check's is the fixture's checkout.

The parallel check pipeline goes: no payload composed in check, no separate
source waiter, no faked menu counts. Tests that drew a composed payload
without a renderer take it from test-side helpers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor(daemon): a payload's owners are typed by what it calls, and the runs a test holds go through a real collector (9a7)

Each owner a payload reads is a Pick of the methods it calls, so a fixture
world types without casts and the daemon's providers still satisfy it. The
tests that held runs through check's holder now hold them through a
collector over the case's source runs, so nothing but check reads that
holder.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(renderer): a segment's error reaches the ⚠ list and the turn record, and each record notes the faults it met (9a7)

A placement that cannot draw still draws its ⚠ cell, and its whole message
is now a `segment` warning among the warnings the draw returns. The renderer
keeps those for the bar's ⚠ list, so the next frame counts it and its viewer
shows it in full. The observer that only `check` passed is gone: check reads
segment warnings from the draw like every other kind.

Each draw's turn record gains two fields:
- `faults`: every error and warning the frame met, each with its level, its
  kind, what it is about where it carries one, and its whole message, as a
  JSON array. It holds `kept` while the list equals the one last noted for
  the session and renderer, so an unchanged bar adds no message per tick.
  The kinds come from the producers' own unions; the draw's errors name
  theirs once. The shared note module spells and parses the note, so host
  code can read what the renderer noted.
- `preset`: the preset the draw used.

`warn=`, `err=`, `diag=` and `warnRecord=` are unchanged; `warn=` tags a
segment warning `segment:<placement>`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
